section_47_late_fee.description: Late fee for delayed filing of GST returns
section_47_late_fee.gstr_3b_with_liability: Rs. 50 per day (Rs. 25 CGST + Rs. 25 SGST), maximum Rs. 5,000
section_47_late_fee.gstr_3b_nil_return: Rs. 20 per day (Rs. 10 CGST + Rs. 10 SGST), maximum Rs. 500
section_47_late_fee.gstr_1_with_liability: Rs. 50 per day (Rs. 25 CGST + Rs. 25 SGST), maximum Rs. 10,000
section_47_late_fee.gstr_1_nil_return: Rs. 20 per day (Rs. 10 CGST + Rs. 10 SGST), maximum Rs. 500
section_47_late_fee.gstr_9_annual_return: Rs. 200 per day (Rs. 100 CGST + Rs. 100 SGST), maximum 0.25% of aggregate turnover
section_47_late_fee.legal_ref: Section 47 of CGST Act read with Notification No. 19/2021-Central Tax

section_50_interest.description: Interest on delayed payment of tax
section_50_interest.rate_normal_per_annum: 18% per annum on delayed payment of self-assessed output tax
section_50_interest.rate_wrong_itc_per_annum: 24% per annum on wrong availment and utilisation of Input Tax Credit
section_50_interest.legal_ref: Section 50(1) and Section 50(3) of CGST Act 2017

section_122_penalty.description: Penalty for tax evasion and offences
section_122_penalty.non_fraud_penalty: Higher of Rs. 10,000 or 10% of tax due
section_122_penalty.fraud_penalty: Higher of Rs. 10,000 or 100% of tax evaded (equal to full tax amount)
section_122_penalty.voluntary_before_scn: 15% of tax due — full penalty waiver available (Section 74(5))

e_way_bill_threshold.inter_state_threshold: Rs. 50,000 — mandatory for all inter-state movement of goods
e_way_bill_threshold.intra_state_threshold: Rs. 50,000 — mandatory (states may notify a different limit)
e_way_bill_threshold.validity_normal_cargo: 1 day for every 200 km or part thereof
e_way_bill_threshold.validity_over_dimensional: 1 day for every 20 km or part thereof
e_way_bill_threshold.exemptions: Goods transported by non-motorised vehicles; goods under customs supervision; goods moved within port/airport/customs bonded area; specific exempt goods per Annexure to Rule 138

registration_threshold.description: Aggregate turnover threshold for mandatory GST registration
registration_threshold.special_category_states_10_lakh: Rs. 10 Lakh — Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura
registration_threshold.special_category_states_20_lakh: Rs. 20 Lakh — Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Puducherry, Sikkim, Telangana, Uttarakhand (for services)
registration_threshold.mandatory_regardless_of_turnover: Inter-state taxable supplier; e-commerce operator; casual taxable person; non-resident taxable person; TDS/TCS deductor
registration_threshold.legal_ref: Section 22 of CGST Act read with Notification No. 10/2019-Central Tax

blocked_credits_17_5.description: Complete negative list for Input Tax Credit — Blocked Credits under Section 17(5)
blocked_credits_17_5.motor_vehicles: Motor vehicles for transportation of persons with approved seating capacity NOT MORE THAN 13 persons — BLOCKED. EXCEPTIONS: used for (a) further supply of such motor vehicles; (b) transportation of passengers; (c) imparting training on driving
blocked_credits_17_5.vessels_aircraft: Vessels and aircraft — BLOCKED. Same three exceptions as motor vehicles apply
blocked_credits_17_5.insurance_maintenance: General insurance, servicing, repair and maintenance on motor vehicles/vessels/aircraft WHEN credit on such vehicle is blocked — ALSO BLOCKED
blocked_credits_17_5.food_beverages: Food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, cosmetic/plastic surgery — BLOCKED. EXCEPTION: where obligatory under any law or used to make same category of taxable outward supply
blocked_credits_17_5.club_membership: Membership of a club, health and fitness centre — BLOCKED (no exception available)
blocked_credits_17_5.rent_a_cab: Rent-a-cab services — BLOCKED. EXCEPTION: obligatory under any law for employees
blocked_credits_17_5.life_health_insurance: Life insurance and health insurance — BLOCKED. EXCEPTION: obligatory under any law
blocked_credits_17_5.travel_benefits: Travel benefits extended to employees on vacation such as Leave Travel Allowance (LTA), Home Travel Concession (HTC) — BLOCKED
blocked_credits_17_5.works_contract_immovable: Works contract services for construction of an immovable property (including a road, bridge, railway, etc.) — BLOCKED. EXCEPTION: plant and machinery
blocked_credits_17_5.own_construction: Goods/services received for construction of immovable property on OWN ACCOUNT — BLOCKED even for furtherance of business. EXCEPTION: plant and machinery
blocked_credits_17_5.legal_ref: Section 17(5) of CGST Act 2017 (as amended by CGST Amendment Act 2018)

section_16_itc_conditions.description: Four mandatory conditions to claim Input Tax Credit
section_16_itc_conditions.condition_1: Possession of a valid tax invoice, debit note, or other prescribed document issued by registered supplier
section_16_itc_conditions.condition_2: Goods or services or both have been received (receipt-based credit — delivery to any person on direction of registered person also counts)
section_16_itc_conditions.condition_3: Tax charged on such supply has actually been paid to the government by the supplier (verified via GSTR-2B)
section_16_itc_conditions.condition_4: The registered person has furnished the return under Section 39 (GSTR-3B filed)
section_16_itc_conditions.180_day_reversal_rule: If payment not made to supplier within 180 days of invoice date — ITC must be reversed along with interest at 18% per annum; can be re-availed once payment is made
section_16_itc_conditions.capital_goods_itc: Full ITC on capital goods allowed in the year of receipt — no spreading over years required

section_16_4_itc_time_limit.description: Deadline for availing Input Tax Credit on invoices
section_16_4_itc_time_limit.rule: ITC in respect of any invoice or debit note must be availed by the EARLIER of: (a) due date of furnishing return under Section 39 for the month of September following the end of the financial year to which such invoice pertains, OR (b) actual date of furnishing of the annual return
section_16_4_itc_time_limit.practical_example: For an invoice dated July 2023 (FY 2023-24): ITC must be claimed in GSTR-3B filed by 20th October 2024 (September 2024 return) OR by the date GSTR-9 for FY 2023-24 is filed — whichever is earlier

time_of_supply_goods.description: Point of taxation for supply of goods
time_of_supply_goods.forward_charge_rule: Earlier of: (a) date of issue of invoice by supplier; OR (b) last date on which he is required to issue invoice under Section 31
time_of_supply_goods.reverse_charge_rule: Earlier of: (a) date of receipt of goods; (b) date of payment; (c) 31st day from date of issue of invoice by supplier

time_of_supply_services.description: Point of taxation for supply of services
time_of_supply_services.forward_charge_rule: Earlier of: (a) date of issue of invoice; OR (b) date of receipt of payment
time_of_supply_services.reverse_charge_rule: Earlier of: (a) date of payment; OR (b) 61st day from date of issue of invoice by supplier

rcm_services.description: Services mandatorily under Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)
rcm_services.gta: Goods Transport Agency (GTA) services — registered recipient pays GST under RCM at 5% (no ITC) or 12% (with ITC)
rcm_services.legal_advocate: Legal services by an advocate/firm to a business entity — RCM on the business entity recipient
rcm_services.director: Services by a director of a company/body corporate to the company — RCM on company
rcm_services.insurance_agent: Services by an insurance agent — RCM on the insurance company
rcm_services.recovery_agent: Services by a recovery agent to a banking company/NBFC — RCM
rcm_services.author_copyright: Supply of copyright in original literary/music/art work by author/composer to publisher — RCM
rcm_services.sponsorship: Sponsorship services provided to any body corporate or partnership firm — RCM on recipient
rcm_services.government_services: Services supplied by government/local authority to a registered business entity — RCM (specific exemptions apply)
rcm_services.security_services: Security services (other than provided by individuals) to registered person — RCM
rcm_services.import_of_services: Import of services from any person outside India — ALWAYS under RCM (Section 5(3) of IGST Act), even if the foreign supplier is unregistered
rcm_services.legal_ref: Notification No. 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate); Section 9(3) CGST Act 2017

section_54_refund.description: Time limit and mechanism for GST refund
section_54_refund.relevant_date_exports_with_igst: Date of dispatch of goods / date of loading on vessel / date on airway bill
section_54_refund.relevant_date_exports_without_tax: End of the quarter in which the export invoice was issued
section_54_refund.relevant_date_unutilized_itc: End of the tax period in which the credit has accumulated
section_54_refund.relevant_date_excess_payment: Date of payment of tax in excess
section_54_refund.zero_rated_exports: Full refund of unutilised ITC allowed for zero-rated supplies (exports and SEZ) — no inverted duty restriction applies
section_54_refund.igst_refund_exports: IGST paid on export of goods is automatically refunded via customs (ICEGATE) on filing of shipping bill — no separate refund application if EGM filed
section_54_refund.legal_ref: Section 54 of CGST Act 2017; Rule 89 of CGST Rules

composition_scheme.description: GST Composition Scheme rates, limits and restrictions
composition_scheme.turnover_limit_goods_traders: Rs. 1.5 Crore aggregate turnover in preceding FY for manufacturers and traders (Rs. 75 Lakh for special category states notified under Section 10)
composition_scheme.turnover_limit_services: Rs. 50 Lakh aggregate turnover for service providers under Section 10(2A)
composition_scheme.rate_manufacturers_traders: 1% of turnover in State (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST)
composition_scheme.rate_service_providers: 6% of turnover (3% CGST + 3% SGST) — applicable to persons supplying services other than restaurant
composition_scheme.restrictions: CANNOT: make inter-state outward supplies; supply exempted goods; collect GST from customers; claim ITC; issue tax invoice; supply through e-commerce operators (except restaurant services)
composition_scheme.legal_ref: Section 10 of CGST Act 2017 read with Notification No. 14/2019-Central Tax

gst_rates_key_goods.description: GST rates on commonly queried goods
gst_rates_key_goods.nil_0_percent: NIL RATE: Fresh fruits, fresh vegetables, milk (liquid), eggs, fish (fresh/dried), meat (unprocessed, non-frozen), cereals, pulses (whole), bread, salt, stamps, judicial papers, bangles (glass/lac), khadi fabric
gst_rates_key_goods.rate_5_percent: 5%: Sugar, edible oils, tea, coffee (not roasted), coal, domestic LPG (for household use), kerosene under PDS, fertilisers, cashew nuts, footwear up to Rs. 1,000, handloom fabrics, fish (frozen), ayurvedic medicines
gst_rates_key_goods.rate_12_percent: 12%: Processed/frozen meat, butter, ghee, cheese, dry fruits (except cashew), mobile phones (smartphones), exercise books, umbrellas, sewing machines, electric vehicles
gst_rates_key_goods.rate_18_percent: 18%: Most capital goods, industrial machinery, computers, monitors, cameras, refrigerators (below 200L excluded), paints, detergents, plastics, steel fabricated structures, most IT hardware/software products
gst_rates_key_goods.rate_28_percent: 28%: Motor vehicles for passengers with approved seating capacity of NOT MORE THAN 13 persons (plus cess), two-wheelers above 350cc (plus cess), large screen TVs (>32 inches), washing machines, dishwashers, ACs, vacuum cleaners, cement, pan masala, aerated drinks, cigarettes, tobacco (plus cess)
gst_rates_key_goods.legal_ref: Schedules I to IV of Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and amendments

gst_rates_key_services.description: GST rates on commonly queried services
gst_rates_key_services.exempt_nil: EXEMPT (NIL): Healthcare by clinical establishments/authorised medical practitioners/paramedics; educational services up to higher secondary; residential dwelling renting; auto-rickshaw/e-rickshaw passenger transport; agriculture support services; religious services
gst_rates_key_services.rate_5_percent: 5%: Standalone restaurant services (AC or non-AC); air travel economy class; rail transport of goods; job work on food/agricultural produce; GTA services (without ITC option)
gst_rates_key_services.rate_12_percent: 12%: Restaurant with liquor license (AC); construction of residential complex for sale (with land deduction); business class air travel; GTA services (with ITC option)
gst_rates_key_services.rate_18_percent: 18%: IT/software services; banking, finance, insurance (most); telecom services; hotel accommodation above Rs. 7,500 per night; professional services (CA, lawyer, architect, consultant); commercial property renting; most services not specifically classified elsewhere
gst_rates_key_services.rate_28_percent: 28%: Gambling, betting in casinos; horse racing clubs; online gaming with wagering; luxury hotel accommodation (five-star category)
gst_rates_key_services.legal_ref: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

section_73_74_demand.description: Time limits for Show Cause Notice (SCN) and adjudication orders
section_73_74_demand.section_73_non_fraud_scn: SCN must be issued within 2 years 9 months from due date of annual return for the relevant FY (i.e., within 33 months)
section_73_74_demand.section_73_non_fraud_order: Order must be issued within 3 years from due date of annual return
section_73_74_demand.section_74_fraud_scn: SCN must be issued within 4 years 6 months from due date of annual return for the relevant FY (i.e., within 54 months)
section_73_74_demand.section_74_fraud_order: Order must be issued within 5 years from due date of annual return
section_73_74_demand.section_74_penalty: Penalty equal to 100% of tax evaded — reducible on voluntary compliance

place_of_supply_services.description: Place of supply rules for services (determines CGST/SGST vs IGST)
place_of_supply_services.b2b_general_rule: Section 12(2)(a): Location of the RECIPIENT of service — applies when recipient is a registered person
place_of_supply_services.b2c_general_rule: Section 12(2)(b): Location of the SUPPLIER of service — applies when recipient is unregistered
place_of_supply_services.immovable_property: Section 12(3): Location of the immovable property — overrides general rule
place_of_supply_services.restaurant_event: Location where service is actually performed / event is held
place_of_supply_services.transport_of_goods: B2B: Location of the registered recipient; B2C: Location at which goods are handed over for transport
place_of_supply_services.cross_border_services: Section 13: Location of the RECIPIENT of services (India is taxable if recipient is in India)

zero_rated_supply.definition: Zero-rated supply means: (a) export of goods or services outside India; OR (b) supply to a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) developer or unit
zero_rated_supply.option_1_with_tax_refund: Export WITH payment of IGST under Bond — claim full refund of IGST paid at time of export
zero_rated_supply.option_2_lut_itc_refund: Export UNDER LETTER OF UNDERTAKING (LUT) without payment of IGST — claim refund of unutilised ITC at end of tax period
zero_rated_supply.lut_eligibility: All GST registered exporters can file LUT EXCEPT those prosecuted for tax evasion exceeding Rs. 2.5 Crore
zero_rated_supply.lut_validity: LUT is valid for the entire financial year in which filed
zero_rated_supply.igst_auto_refund: IGST paid on export of GOODS is auto-refunded via ICEGATE-GSTN data exchange when shipping bill is filed correctly
zero_rated_supply.legal_ref: Section 16 of IGST Act 2017; Rule 89 and Rule 96 of CGST Rules

annual_return.who_must_file_gstr9: All registered taxpayers EXCEPT: composition dealers (file GSTR-9A); casual taxable persons; Input Service Distributors; non-resident taxable persons; TDS/TCS deductors
annual_return.gstr_9c_mandatory_threshold: Taxpayers with aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 5 Crore in the relevant FY must file GSTR-9C (self-certified reconciliation statement)
annual_return.due_date: 31st December following the end of the relevant financial year
annual_return.legal_ref: Section 44 of CGST Act 2017; Rule 80 of CGST Rules

gst_on_real_estate.description: GST rates on real estate and construction
gst_on_real_estate.affordable_housing: 1% (WITHOUT ITC) — affordable residential apartments: value up to Rs. 45 Lakh AND carpet area up to 60 sqm in metro cities / 90 sqm in non-metro cities
gst_on_real_estate.other_residential: 5% (WITHOUT ITC) — other under-construction residential apartments (not affordable housing)
gst_on_real_estate.commercial_construction: 12% (WITHOUT ITC) — commercial properties under construction sold before Completion Certificate
gst_on_real_estate.completed_property_no_gst: NO GST — sale of completed / ready-to-move-in property (where Completion Certificate has been issued) is not a supply; exempt from GST
gst_on_real_estate.pure_works_contract: 12% (WITH ITC) — construction services not involving transfer of property rights (e.g., contractor building for a business)
gst_on_real_estate.legal_ref: Notification No. 03/2019-Central Tax (Rate); Entry 3(i), 3(ia), 3(ib) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

gst_on_healthcare_education.description: GST applicability on healthcare and education
gst_on_healthcare_education.healthcare_exempt: EXEMPT: Services by a clinical establishment, authorised medical practitioner, or paramedic — including inpatient/outpatient treatment, diagnostic tests, ambulance services
gst_on_healthcare_education.healthcare_taxable_18: TAXABLE at 18%: Cosmetic or plastic surgery not medically necessary; health club/gym memberships; weight loss programmes
gst_on_healthcare_education.education_exempt: EXEMPT: Services by an educational institution to its students/faculty/staff — covers pre-school through higher secondary school (Class 12) and equivalent; also includes affiliated/recognised colleges up to degree level
gst_on_healthcare_education.education_taxable_18: TAXABLE at 18%: Private coaching classes not affiliated with a recognised university/board; online professional courses by non-educational institutions; skill development (other than government-notified schemes)

section_129_130_detention.description: Detention, seizure and release of goods in transit
section_129_130_detention.owner_comes_forward_taxable: 200% of the tax payable on the goods — penalty for taxable goods where owner comes forward
section_129_130_detention.owner_not_coming_forward_taxable: Higher of 50% of the value of goods OR 200% of tax payable — where owner does not come forward
section_129_130_detention.exempt_goods_penalty: Lower of 2% of value of goods OR Rs. 25,000
section_129_130_detention.confiscation_section_130: Fine in lieu of confiscation not less than tax amount — applicable where goods liable to confiscation

input_service_distributor.description: Input Service Distributor (ISD) — credit distribution mechanism
input_service_distributor.definition: ISD is an office of the supplier (usually head office) that receives invoices for input services and distributes the ITC to its branches/units having the same PAN
input_service_distributor.distribution_basis: ITC distributed pro-rata based on turnover of each branch in the period during which credit is being distributed
input_service_distributor.restriction: ISD can ONLY distribute credit of INPUT SERVICES — credit of goods and capital goods CANNOT be distributed via ISD
input_service_distributor.legal_ref: Section 20 of CGST Act 2017; Rule 39 of CGST Rules 2017

tds_gst.description: Tax Deducted at Source under GST
tds_gst.rate: 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST/UTGST) of the payment made to the supplier
tds_gst.threshold: Applicable when total value of supply under a contract exceeds Rs. 2,50,000 (excluding tax)
tds_gst.who_deducts: Central/State Government departments; local authorities; government agencies; persons notified under Section 51
tds_gst.return: GSTR-7 — monthly return by deductor, due by 10th of the following month

tcs_gst.description: Tax Collected at Source by E-Commerce Operators
tcs_gst.rate: 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST/UTGST) of the net value of taxable supplies made through the e-commerce platform
tcs_gst.net_value: Aggregate value of taxable supplies MINUS returns — TCS is calculated on net taxable value
tcs_gst.return: GSTR-8 — monthly return by e-commerce operator, due by 10th of the following month

section_15_valuation.description: Value of taxable supply (transaction value rules)
section_15_valuation.transaction_value: The price actually paid or payable for the supply of goods or services or both, WHERE the supplier and recipient are NOT related and price is the sole consideration
section_15_valuation.inclusions: Transaction value INCLUDES: (a) taxes/duties other than GST; (b) interest, late fee, penalty for delayed payment; (c) incidental expenses charged (packing, commission, etc.); (d) subsidies directly linked to price (except government subsidies); (e) amounts recharged by supplier
section_15_valuation.exclusions: EXCLUDES: (a) discount BEFORE or at the time of supply if recorded on invoice face; (b) discount AFTER supply if established by agreement at time of supply, linked to specific invoices, and ITC reversed by recipient proportionately
section_15_valuation.legal_ref: Section 15 of CGST Act 2017; Rules 27-35 of CGST Rules

section_31_invoice_rules.goods_before_removal: Invoice for goods must be issued BEFORE or at the time of removal of goods (for supply involving movement) or delivery of goods (for supply not involving movement)
section_31_invoice_rules.services_within_30_days: Invoice for services must be issued within 30 days from the date of supply of service (45 days for banking/financial/insurance company)
section_31_invoice_rules.continuous_supply_goods: Invoice at the time of each successive statement of accounts or before each payment receipt
section_31_invoice_rules.continuous_supply_services: Invoice before the due date of payment or before the receipt of payment, whichever is earlier
section_31_invoice_rules.legal_ref: Section 31 of CGST Act 2017; Rule 46 of CGST Rules

section_34_credit_debit_notes.description: Credit notes and debit notes under GST
section_34_credit_debit_notes.credit_note_when: When tax invoice has been issued and: (a) taxable value or tax charged exceeds the actual amount; (b) goods are returned by recipient; (c) goods/services found deficient
section_34_credit_debit_notes.debit_note_when: When tax invoice has been issued and taxable value or tax charged is LESS than the actual amount payable
section_34_credit_debit_notes.credit_note_time_limit: Must be declared in return filed for the month of September following end of FY in which supply was made, OR date of filing annual return — whichever is earlier
section_34_credit_debit_notes.itc_reversal: Recipient must reverse ITC to the extent of the credit note amount in the tax period in which credit note is received

section_17_1_2_apportionment.description: ITC apportionment between business and non-business, taxable and exempt
section_17_1_2_apportionment.section_17_1: Where goods or services are used PARTLY for business and PARTLY for non-business purposes — ITC allowed ONLY to the extent attributable to business purposes
section_17_1_2_apportionment.section_17_2: Where goods or services are used PARTLY for taxable supplies (including zero-rated) and PARTLY for exempt supplies — ITC allowed ONLY to the extent attributable to taxable supplies
section_17_1_2_apportionment.rule_42_services: Common credit for input services reversed using Rule 42 formula: D2 = (E/F) x C2, where E=exempt turnover, F=total turnover, C2=common credit after direct attribution
section_17_1_2_apportionment.rule_43_capital_goods: Common credit for capital goods reversed using Rule 43: monthly reversal = Tr/Tm, where Tr=exempt turnover in that tax period, Tm=total turnover in that tax period
section_17_1_2_apportionment.legal_ref: Sections 17(1) and 17(2) of CGST Act 2017; Rules 42 and 43 of CGST Rules

rule_86b_itc_restriction.description: Restriction on use of ITC for payment of output tax
rule_86b_itc_restriction.rule: Registered person having taxable supply value (other than exempt and zero-rated) exceeding Rs. 50 Lakh in a month MUST pay at least 1% of output tax liability in cash (through electronic cash ledger)
rule_86b_itc_restriction.exceptions: Does NOT apply if: (a) head of GST paid > Rs. 1 Lakh in preceding FY; (b) registered person received refund > Rs. 1 Lakh under zero-rated; (c) cumulative tax paid using ECL exceeds 1% of total output; (d) person is government department/PSU/local authority

section_9_4_rcm_unregistered.description: RCM on supply from unregistered person
section_9_4_rcm_unregistered.current_position: Section 9(4) RCM on ALL supplies from unregistered persons is currently SUSPENDED for all categories EXCEPT specified notified categories
section_9_4_rcm_unregistered.notified_categories: RCM applies on procurement from unregistered persons ONLY for: (a) specified goods like cashew nuts, bidi wrapper leaves, tobacco leaves, silk yarn; (b) cement from unregistered manufacturers
section_9_4_rcm_unregistered.legal_ref: Section 9(4) of CGST Act 2017; Notification No. 07/2019-Central Tax (Rate)

anti_profiteering.rule: Any reduction in rate of tax or benefit of ITC MUST be passed on to the recipient by way of commensurate reduction in prices
anti_profiteering.authority: Complaints investigated by DGAP (Director General of Anti-Profiteering) and adjudicated by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) — took over from NAA w.e.f. 01.12.2022
anti_profiteering.penalty: Penalty of 10% of the profiteered amount; if not passed on, amount deposited in Consumer Welfare Fund
anti_profiteering.legal_ref: Section 171 of CGST Act 2017; Rule 127-137 of CGST Rules

section_83_provisional_attachment.description: Provisional attachment of property to protect revenue
section_83_provisional_attachment.when: Commissioner may provisionally attach (including bank account) property of a taxable person DURING pendency of any proceeding under Section 62, 63, 64, 67, 73, or 74
section_83_provisional_attachment.duration: Attachment ceases to have effect after 1 year from the date of the order
section_83_provisional_attachment.safeguard: Must form opinion that it is necessary to protect revenue — cannot be used as a coercive measure for tax collection

section_107_appeal_first.time_limit: Appeal within 3 months from date of communication of the order (or decision)
section_107_appeal_first.condonation: Appellate Authority may condone delay up to 1 month beyond the 3-month period (total 4 months — NOT beyond)
section_107_appeal_first.pre_deposit: Mandatory pre-deposit: (a) full amount of tax, interest, fine, fee, and penalty ADMITTED by appellant; PLUS (b) 10% of the DISPUTED tax amount
section_107_appeal_first.cap_on_pre_deposit: Pre-deposit of disputed tax capped at Rs. 25 Crore (CGST) + Rs. 25 Crore (SGST) = Rs. 50 Crore combined

section_112_appeal_tribunal.time_limit: Appeal within 3 months from date of communication of the order of Appellate Authority
section_112_appeal_tribunal.condonation: Tribunal may condone delay up to 3 months beyond the 3-month period (total 6 months — NOT beyond)
section_112_appeal_tribunal.pre_deposit: Mandatory pre-deposit: (a) full amount of admitted tax; PLUS (b) 20% of the REMAINING disputed tax (over and above 10% paid at first appeal stage)
section_112_appeal_tribunal.cap_on_pre_deposit: Pre-deposit of disputed tax capped at Rs. 50 Crore (CGST) + Rs. 50 Crore (SGST) = Rs. 100 Crore combined

section_73_voluntary_compliance.description: Voluntary payment before/after SCN to reduce penalty (non-fraud cases)
section_73_voluntary_compliance.before_scn_73_5: Pay tax + interest BEFORE issuance of SCN — NO penalty, NO SCN issued
section_73_voluntary_compliance.within_30_days_of_scn_73_8: Pay tax + interest + 10% penalty within 30 days of SCN — proceedings concluded

section_74_voluntary_compliance.description: Voluntary payment before/after SCN to reduce penalty (fraud/suppression cases)
section_74_voluntary_compliance.before_scn_74_5: Pay tax + interest + 15% penalty BEFORE issuance of SCN — NO further proceedings
section_74_voluntary_compliance.within_30_days_of_scn_74_6: Pay tax + interest + 25% penalty within 30 days of SCN — proceedings concluded
section_74_voluntary_compliance.within_30_days_of_order_74_7: Pay tax + interest + 50% penalty within 30 days of order — reduced penalty

gst_on_gold_jewellery.description: GST on gold, precious metals and jewellery
gst_on_gold_jewellery.gold_bars_coins: 3% GST on gold bars, gold coins, gold ornaments (HSN 7108, 7113)
gst_on_gold_jewellery.making_charges: 5% GST on job work services (making charges) for gold jewellery
gst_on_gold_jewellery.silver: 3% GST on silver bars, silver articles
gst_on_gold_jewellery.diamonds: 0.25% GST on rough diamonds; 3% on cut and polished diamonds
gst_on_gold_jewellery.legal_ref: Entry 2 of Schedule I and Entry 13 of Schedule II of Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

gst_on_ecommerce.description: GST provisions for e-commerce operators and sellers
gst_on_ecommerce.section_52_tcs: E-commerce operator must collect TCS at 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST) of net value of intra-state supplies
gst_on_ecommerce.section_9_5: E-commerce operator liable to pay tax on notified services: (a) hotel accommodation; (b) housekeeping; (c) restaurant services through e-commerce platform
gst_on_ecommerce.mandatory_registration: E-commerce operators must obtain GST registration irrespective of turnover — Section 24(x)
gst_on_ecommerce.sellers_on_platform: Suppliers selling through e-commerce platforms must also obtain registration irrespective of turnover — Section 24(ix), EXCEPT suppliers of goods with turnover up to Rs. 40 Lakh notified under Section 10(2A)

gst_on_rent.commercial_property: 18% GST on renting of commercial immovable property (shops, offices, warehouses, godowns)
gst_on_rent.residential_property_unregistered: EXEMPT when rented for RESIDENTIAL purpose to an UNREGISTERED person
gst_on_rent.residential_property_registered_rcm: 18% GST under RCM when residential property is rented to a REGISTERED person (w.e.f. 18.07.2022 per Notification No. 05/2022)
gst_on_rent.hotel_below_1000: EXEMPT: Hotel/guest house/inn with declared tariff below Rs. 1,000 per day
gst_on_rent.legal_ref: Entry 13 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate); Notification No. 05/2022-Central Tax (Rate)

gst_on_freight.description: GST on freight and transportation of goods
gst_on_freight.gta_5_no_itc: 5% GST (forward charge) — GTA option where transporter pays GST but cannot claim ITC
gst_on_freight.gta_12_with_itc: 12% GST (forward charge) — GTA option where transporter pays GST and CAN claim ITC
gst_on_freight.gta_rcm_5: 5% GST under RCM — specified recipients pay tax: factory, society, cooperative, registered person, body corporate, partnership firm, casual taxable person
gst_on_freight.rail_transport: 5% GST on transport of goods by rail (Indian Railways)
gst_on_freight.vessel_transport: 5% GST on transport of goods by vessel (inland waterway / coastal)
gst_on_freight.exempt_goods_transport: EXEMPT: Transport of agricultural produce, milk, salt, food grains, newspaper, organic manure, defence equipment, relief goods
gst_on_freight.legal_ref: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) as amended; Notification No. 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

inverted_duty_structure.description: Refund for inverted duty structure (input tax rate > output tax rate)
inverted_duty_structure.rule: Refund of accumulated ITC allowed when rate of tax on inputs is HIGHER than rate of tax on output supplies — creates accumulation of ITC
inverted_duty_structure.formula: Maximum refund = (Turnover of inverted rated supply x Net ITC / Adjusted total turnover) - Tax payable on inverted rated supply
inverted_duty_structure.not_allowed: Refund NOT allowed for: (a) goods notified under Section 54(3) proviso (tobacco, pan masala); (b) ITC accumulated on input services (only on inputs — goods)
inverted_duty_structure.legal_ref: Section 54(3) of CGST Act 2017; Rule 89(5) of CGST Rules

section_9_1_levy_and_collection.cgst: CGST levied on all intra-state supplies of goods/services at the rate notified, not exceeding 20%, collected by Central Government
section_9_1_levy_and_collection.sgst: SGST levied on all intra-state supplies at the rate notified, not exceeding 20%, collected by respective State Government
section_9_1_levy_and_collection.igst: IGST levied on all inter-state supplies at the rate notified, not exceeding 40%, collected by Central Government
section_9_1_levy_and_collection.cess: Compensation Cess levied under GST Compensation Cess Act 2017 on notified luxury and sin goods (motor vehicles, tobacco, aerated drinks, coal)
section_9_1_levy_and_collection.legal_ref: Section 9(1) CGST Act; Section 5(1) IGST Act; Section 8 GST Compensation Cess Act

section_2_supply_definition.definition: Supply includes: (a) sale; (b) transfer; (c) barter; (d) exchange; (e) licence; (f) rental; (g) lease; (h) disposal — made or agreed to be made for a consideration by a person in the course or furtherance of business
section_2_supply_definition.schedule_i_without_consideration: Taxable even WITHOUT consideration: (a) permanent transfer of business assets where ITC was claimed; (b) supply between related/distinct persons in course of business; (c) supply by principal to agent or vice versa; (d) importation of services from related person even without consideration
section_2_supply_definition.schedule_ii_deemed_supply: Specific activities deemed supply of goods or services: transfer of title = goods; transfer of right to use without title = service; works contract = service; restaurant/catering = service; software temporary transfer = service
section_2_supply_definition.composite_supply: Section 2(30): Supply of 2+ goods/services which are naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business — taxed at rate of PRINCIPAL supply
section_2_supply_definition.mixed_supply: Section 2(74): Supply of 2+ goods/services NOT naturally bundled — taxed at the HIGHEST rate applicable to any of the constituent supplies
section_2_supply_definition.legal_ref: Section 7 and Schedule I, II, III of CGST Act 2017; Sections 2(30) and 2(74)

section_49_payment_of_tax.description: Payment of tax and utilisation order of ITC
section_49_payment_of_tax.utilisation_order: IGST credit must be used FIRST against IGST liability; remaining IGST credit can be set off against CGST then SGST in any order. CGST credit: used against CGST first, then IGST (NOT against SGST). SGST credit: used against SGST first, then IGST (NOT against CGST)
section_49_payment_of_tax.electronic_cash_ledger: All deposits of cash (through challans) credited here. Used for payment of tax, interest, penalty, fees, etc.
section_49_payment_of_tax.electronic_credit_ledger: All ITC credited here. Can only be used for payment of output tax — NOT for interest, penalty, or fees
section_49_payment_of_tax.legal_ref: Section 49 of CGST Act 2017; Rule 88A of CGST Rules

section_39_returns.description: GST returns filing requirements and due dates
section_39_returns.gstr_1_due_date: 11th of the following month — details of outward supplies
section_39_returns.gstr_1_quarterly: 13th of the month following the quarter — for taxpayers under QRMP scheme (turnover up to Rs. 5 Crore)
section_39_returns.gstr_3b_due_date: 20th of the following month — summary return with tax payment
section_39_returns.gstr_3b_quarterly: 22nd/24th of the month following the quarter — for QRMP scheme taxpayers
section_39_returns.qrmp_threshold: Taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to Rs. 5 Crore in preceding FY can opt for Quarterly Return Monthly Payment (QRMP) scheme
section_39_returns.legal_ref: Section 39 of CGST Act 2017; Notification No. 29/2020-Central Tax

section_70_summons.description: Power to summon persons and compel production of documents
section_70_summons.power: Proper officer may summon any person whose attendance is necessary for giving evidence or producing a document or any other thing during inquiry or proceedings
section_70_summons.penalty_for_non_compliance: Person summoned who fails to attend or produce documents without reasonable cause may be prosecuted

section_67_inspection_search_seizure.description: Power of inspection, search and seizure under GST
section_67_inspection_search_seizure.inspection_67_1: Joint Commissioner or above can authorise inspection of any place of business of a taxable person or transporter/warehouse owner where there is reason to believe tax evasion
section_67_inspection_search_seizure.search_and_seizure_67_2: Joint Commissioner or above can authorize SEARCH if he has reason to BELIEVE that goods liable to confiscation, documents/books useful for proceedings are secreted
section_67_inspection_search_seizure.seizure_duration: Seized goods must be returned within 6 months (extendable by 6 months by Commissioner) if no notice issued under Section 73/74

section_35_36_accounts_records.description: Accounts and records to be maintained by registered person
section_35_36_accounts_records.records_required: Every registered person must maintain: production/manufacture records; inward/outward supply records; stock records; ITC availed; output tax payable/paid; other prescribed records
section_35_36_accounts_records.retention_period: All accounts/records must be retained until the expiry of 72 months (6 years) from the due date of filing of annual return for the year to which records pertain
section_35_36_accounts_records.legal_ref: Sections 35 and 36 of CGST Act 2017; Rule 56 of CGST Rules

section_61_scrutiny.description: Scrutiny of returns by proper officer
section_61_scrutiny.process: Proper officer may scrutinise return to verify its correctness and inform the registered person of any discrepancy via Form GST ASMT-10
section_61_scrutiny.response_time: Registered person must respond within 30 days of receipt of notice (or further period as extended)
section_61_scrutiny.if_unsatisfactory: If explanation is unsatisfactory, proper officer may initiate appropriate action under Section 65 (audit), Section 66 (special audit), Section 73 (demand without fraud), or Section 74 (demand with fraud)

section_62_assessment_non_filer.rule: If a registered person FAILS to file return even after notice under Section 46 — proper officer may assess the tax liability to the BEST OF HIS JUDGEMENT
section_62_assessment_non_filer.withdrawal: Assessment under Section 62 is deemed WITHDRAWN if the registered person files a valid return within 60 days of the assessment order (increased from 30 days by Finance Act 2023)

section_65_audit_by_department.who_can_audit: Commissioner or any officer authorised by him may conduct audit of any registered person
section_65_audit_by_department.notice_period: 15 working days advance notice before conduct of audit
section_65_audit_by_department.completion_time: Audit must be completed within 3 months from date of commencement (extendable by 6 months by Commissioner for reasons recorded in writing)
section_65_audit_by_department.follow_up: If audit reveals discrepancy — proper officer may initiate action under Section 73 or 74

gst_on_insurance.life_insurance_single_premium: 18% on 25% of the premium in 1st year and 12.5% from 2nd year onwards (for unit-linked/investment-linked)
gst_on_insurance.pure_life_risk: 18% on the entire premium for pure term/risk cover life insurance
gst_on_insurance.general_insurance: 18% on the entire premium (motor, fire, marine, travel, health)
gst_on_insurance.reinsurance: 18% on the entire premium for reinsurance services

gst_on_works_contract.definition: Works contract means a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any IMMOVABLE PROPERTY wherein transfer of property in goods is involved in the execution
gst_on_works_contract.government_works: 12% GST on works contract for Central/State Government, local authority, government entity
gst_on_works_contract.private_works: 18% GST on works contract services (other than government works, affordable housing, and specified construction)
gst_on_works_contract.affordable_housing_works: 12% GST on works contract for construction of affordable residential apartments
gst_on_works_contract.itc_blocked_immovable: ITC on works contract is BLOCKED when used for construction of immovable property on own account (Section 17(5)(c)) — EXCEPT plant and machinery
gst_on_works_contract.legal_ref: Section 2(119) of CGST Act 2017; Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

gst_on_job_work.general_rate: 18% GST on job work services (default rate)
gst_on_job_work.manufacturing_rate_12: 12% GST on job work on goods falling under Chapter 71 (jewellery) and any other manufacturing job work
gst_on_job_work.food_agri_rate_5: 5% GST on job work on food products, printing, textiles
gst_on_job_work.time_limit_goods: Inputs sent must be received back within 1 YEAR; capital goods within 3 YEARS — failing which, deemed supply by principal on the date of expiry
gst_on_job_work.principal_registration_rule: Principal can send goods to job worker without payment of tax if goods returned within stipulated time; job worker NOT required to take registration if turnover below threshold
gst_on_job_work.legal_ref: Section 143 of CGST Act 2017; Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

gst_compensation_cess.description: GST Compensation Cess on luxury and sin goods
gst_compensation_cess.motor_vehicles: Cess ranges from 1% to 22% depending on engine capacity, length, and fuel type — e.g., SUVs (length > 4000mm, engine > 1500cc) attract 22% cess
gst_compensation_cess.coal: Rs. 400 per tonne compensation cess on coal, briquettes and similar solid fuels
gst_compensation_cess.aerated_beverages: 12% cess on aerated/carbonated waters with added sugar
gst_compensation_cess.tobacco_pan_masala: Cess varies: Pan masala with tobacco (Gutkha) — 204% of RSP; filter cigarettes — specific + ad-valorem rates; bidis — nil cess
gst_compensation_cess.validity: Compensation Cess was originally levied for 5 years (July 2017 to June 2022) but extended to March 2026 to repay borrowings made during COVID-19
gst_compensation_cess.legal_ref: GST (Compensation to States) Cess Act 2017; Notification No. 1/2017-Compensation Cess (Rate)

section_25_registration_types.normal: Regular registration — valid until cancelled; no expiry
section_25_registration_types.composition: Composition Scheme registration under Section 10 — simplified compliance, quarterly returns
section_25_registration_types.casual_taxable_person: Temporary registration for persons who occasionally undertake transactions in a state where they have no fixed place of business — valid for 90 days (extendable by 90 days)
section_25_registration_types.non_resident_taxable_person: Registration for persons with no fixed establishment in India — valid for 90 days (extendable by 90 days); must pay full estimated tax as advance deposit
section_25_registration_types.voluntary: Person below threshold can voluntarily register — once registered, must comply for at least 1 year before applying for cancellation
section_25_registration_types.suo_motu_cancellation: Proper officer may cancel registration if: (a) person not conducted business from registered place; (b) invoices without supply of goods/services; (c) violates anti-profiteering provisions

section_140_transitional_credit.description: Transitional provisions for ITC carried forward from pre-GST regime
section_140_transitional_credit.tran_1: Registered person entitled to take credit of ITC carried forward in the last return filed under pre-GST law (VAT/Central Excise/Service Tax) — filed in Form TRAN-1
section_140_transitional_credit.deadline: Supreme Court (in Filco Trade Case) allowed filing/revision of TRAN-1 up to 30.11.2022. No further extensions granted
section_140_transitional_credit.legal_ref: Section 140 of CGST Act 2017; SCC judgment in Union of India vs Filco Trade Centre Pvt. Ltd.

gst_on_government_services.description: GST on services by or to Government
gst_on_government_services.exempt_sovereign: EXEMPT: Services by Government/local authority in the nature of sovereign/public functions — e.g., issuance of passports, visas, driving licences, birth/death certificates
gst_on_government_services.taxable_commercial: TAXABLE: Services by Government/local authority of commercial nature — e.g., renting immovable property, postal services (Speed Post, etc.), transport of goods/passengers
gst_on_government_services.rcm_on_recipient: When Government/local authority supplies taxable services to a registered business entity — RCM applies, recipient pays GST
gst_on_government_services.legal_ref: Entry 4, 6 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate); Notification No. 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

gst_on_restaurants_hotels.description: GST rates on restaurants and hotel accommodation
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.standalone_restaurant: 5% GST (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST) — WITHOUT ITC. Applies to all standalone restaurants (AC or non-AC)
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.restaurant_in_hotel_below_7500: 5% GST — restaurant services in hotels with room tariff below Rs. 7,500 per unit per day
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.restaurant_in_hotel_above_7500: 5% GST — restaurant services in hotels with room tariff Rs. 7,500 and above (changed from 18% w.e.f. 01.10.2019)
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.outdoor_catering: 5% GST (WITHOUT ITC) on outdoor catering services other than in premises with daily tariff >= Rs. 7,500
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.hotel_room_below_1000: EXEMPT — room tariff up to Rs. 1,000 per day
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.hotel_room_1001_to_7500: 12% GST on room tariff from Rs. 1,001 to Rs. 7,500 per day
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.hotel_room_above_7500: 18% GST on room tariff above Rs. 7,500 per day
gst_on_restaurants_hotels.legal_ref: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) as amended by Notification No. 20/2019-Central Tax (Rate)
